p: shall come to pass in the: The decree and ordinance of God, concerning the restoration of the Church, which is chiefly meant by the time of Christ.
shall be established on the top: In an evident place to be seen and discerned.
flow to it: When the kingdom of Christ will be enlarged by the preaching of the doctrine. Here also is declared the zeal of the children of God when they are called.
the mountain of the LORD: Alluding to mount Zion, where the visible Church then was.
law: Meaning, the whole doctrine of salvation.
Jerusalem: This was accomplished when the gospel was first preached in Jerusalem, and from there went through all the world.
he shall judge among the nations: The Lord, who is Christ, will have all power given to him.
rebuke many people: That they may acknowledge their sins, and turn to him.
beat their swords into plowshares: He shows the fruit of the peace which the gospel should bring, that is, that men should do good to one another, while before they were enemies.

war any more: He speaks not against the use of weapons and lawful war, but shows how the hearts of the godly will be affected one toward another, which peace and love begin and grow in this life, but will be perfected when we are joined with our head Jesus Christ.
walk in the light of the: Seeing the Gentiles will be ready, make haste, and show them the way to worship God.
hast forsaken thy people the house: The prophet seeing the small hope that the Jews would convert, complains to God as though he had utterly forsaken them for their sins.
filled with customs from the east: Full of the corruptions that reigned chiefly in the east parts.
and they please themselves in the: They altogether gave themselves to the fashions of other nations.
silver and gold: The prophet first condemned their superstition and idolatry next their covetousness and thirdly their vain trust in worldly means.
humbleth himself: He notes the nature of the idolaters who are never satisfied in their superstitions.
forgive them not: Thus the prophet spoke being inflamed with the zeal of God's glory, and that he might fear them with God's judgment.
that day: Meaning, as soon as God will begin to execute his judgments.
mountains: By high trees and mountains are he means the proud and lofty, who think themselves most strong in this world.
all the ships of Tarshish: He condemns their vain confidence which they had in strongholds and in their rich merchandise which brought in vain pleasures with which men's minds became effeminate.
to the moles and to the: They will cast them into vile and filthy places when they perceive that they are not able to help them.
breath is in his nostrils: Cast off your vain confidence in man, whose life is so frail that if his nose is stopped he is dead and consider that you are dealing with God.
